newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha jumps on crude, sentiment firms.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha jumps on crude, sentiment firms.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha prices were sharply higher on Thursday, fuelled by overnight gains in crude prices, traders said.
Market sentiment firmed after a Japanese petrochemical firm on Tuesday bought a first-half March cargo at a high price of about $4.00 above the mean of Singapore quotes, they said.
Open-spec naphtha first-half April was assessed at about $234.50/236.00, up $3.50 from Wednesday levels. Second-half March was assessed about $2.00 above first-half April levels.
The one-month spread from first-half April was assessed at $3.50/4.00 a tad firmer compared to Wednesday's $2.50/4.00.
On Wednesday, second-half April/second-half July switched hands at about $10.50, traders said.
"There aren't so many prompt cargoes in the market," a trader said. "The backwardation may deepen," he said.
About two Japanese petrochemical firms are believed to be potential buyers of second-March cargoes, traders said.

In the low-sulphur waxy residue (LSWR) market, traders said they were waiting for the results of KEPCO's buying tender, before starting talks over Indonesian February cargoes. KEPCO's tender to buy two 500,000-barrel cargoes of LSWR for March delivery closes today. --Tokyo Energy Desk +81-3-5473-3708
